rows.reason: Quotes are on lines 5 and 6 as cited, line 7 has the brush flung down; shows spring reaching into his house and rules out the Rat (not until line 52).
'dulled hearing' starts on line 18 after the long time in the cellarage; correctly puts the change in his ears, not the birds; rabbits are later (line 22).
'impatient and contemptuous' is on line 23; joy of spring is lines 19-20; bowled over (23) and gone (26) are accurate; reaches the key from the evidence.
'spell-bound' is on line 35 within the cited lines 34-35; maps the child-and-storyteller comparison onto the river correctly; 'tired' is later in line 35.
'rather pettishly' is on line 57, 'river and riverside life' on line 58; newness to the river supports the key; boat first seen at line 60 is correct.
'never been in a boat' is in his last words (line 67); river was new (line 29); rules out the oars option; true and teaches the firsts.
'saw only the father' is on line 6; shows the hope (lines 5-6) and what he missed; dance is later. True and in form.
'she began to fear' is on line 14 and 'flying about from one place to another' runs on from it; never settling is line 15; dinner earlier, guests later is correct.
'his fine, tall person' line 27, handsomer line 30, 'ten thousand a year' line 29, Derbyshire line 33: all correct; reaches the key from both pieces of evidence.

Shows only that 'his manners' turned the tide, then concludes 'his behaviour changed the room's mind'. It never shows line 32 ('proud', 'above his company'), which is what makes the key's 'as if he were better than everyone' true, so 'behaviour' does not separate the key from the 'angry that the ball had ended' option (Bingley, line 37). Also 'gave a disgust' is left unexplained.
'slighted one of her daughters' is on lines 45-46 within the cited range; 'slighted' glossed correctly; the cause of the sharpened dislike is shown.
False claim: 'It opens 'I must have you dance''. The speech on line 51 opens with 'Come, Darcy'. Say the speech says 'I must have you dance' and ends 'You had much better dance'. Rest is correct.

Jumps from 'with great spirit' straight to 'So she finds the funny side'. 'With great spirit' does not mean funny; the evidence for the key is lines 72-73 ('lively, playful disposition, which delighted in anything ridiculous'), which the script never shows.
Lines 24-25 have him speak 'helplessly' wishing Marilla were there to cope; shows he cannot face it alone; true and in form.
Afraid he was not coming (line 51), tree plan called 'lovely' (line 55), sure he would come by morning (lines 57-58): all true; shows hard situation turned lovely and rules out the preference option.
Lines 60-61: cannot tell the child about the mistake, will let Marilla do it; shows kindness now and the hard talk later; true.
Lines 24-26: he was frightened, did not turn or run, 'not brought up to that'; leads directly to the key.
Line 34: 'that happened sometimes when the floods were out'; correctly infers the master took it as usual, not danger.
Whip touch and sharp cut are lines 37-38; 'wiser than we were' lines 62-63; sets the two moments side by side before the conclusion.
Handkerchief in the coat (lines 20-21), coat taken off at line 8, whole house switches to the coat (line 22): all correct.
Lines 27-29 list the helpers correctly; four before the fifth passes the hammer; contrasts the crowd with one nail; supports the key.
Lines 6-7 he takes the job on; lines 61-63 he surveys the mess 'with evident pride' and boasts; shows the unchanged confidence.
Lines 15-18 lockers vs sizes, lines 19-22 Whitby vs swimming hat: both correct; shows each reply is about the sorting.
Lines 24-27: he asked if it was far, she laughed and he laughed 'slightly after her'; the late laugh as a mind catching up supports the key.

Concludes 'The same rule is kept for her and broken for him' but never shows the rule: lines 7-8 (named things go in the returns box, unnamed to the charity box). Without that, and without showing the jumper is named (lines 31-32, 46), the child cannot see what rule he broke.
Six sentences; the form allows 3-5. It also ends by restating the key verbatim ('one Reuben is not going to fill') without saying why the empty space points to him.

Lists the evidence (lines 47-49) but never says how it answers the question: nothing says the longer look means she doubts his reason, or that folding it back his way means she lets it stand. The method step is missing.

Retells lines 11-14 only. It never says what 'anyway' shows or that the other choice was the charity box (lines 7-8), so it does not show how to reach 'rather try to return a thing than give it away'.
Line 18 'mustn't think of the garden yet'; 'yet' means later, not never; line 19 puts the work first. True and teaches the key.

'Nobody is in the kitchen at all' is not in the passage; Mother was up and boiled water in a saucepan (line 47). It also skips lines 42-43, where the water boils away and the bottom burns out. Times (5.30 to 8, two and a half hours) are correct.
They look at each other (line 66), same thought (lines 66-67), the thought given at lines 69-70 before anyone speaks; supports the key.
Line 27 'round the house and round the house', stables across the yard (lines 27-28), garden behind the stables (line 72): correct and shows why the search missed it.
Line 17 is its own paragraph and says he told Mum he was going to Ryan's; shows the trip was kept from her and that no reason is given.

Ends by restating the key verbatim ('because it sat higher up than the field beside him') without saying why water higher than the field would make him avoid looking (it is held back only by the bank, which is unsettling). Juxtaposes two lines and announces the answer.
Line 33 water over his boot, line 34 moves back and it comes further, lines 34-35 'not going to stop'; supports 'goes on whatever he does' and rules out the tide going out.
Light going (line 40), both hands and 'even then' the picture shook (line 41); correctly shows two causes and rules out the both-hands option.
Fancies (lines 11-13), horse in the dusk (14-15), Bessie's tales (15), Gytrash coming upon travellers (16-17), 'as this horse was now coming upon me' (17-18): all correct.
Dog like one form of the Gytrash (21-22), horse with a rider (24-25), the man broke the spell (25), only a traveller (25-26): all correct and leads to the key.
